smt-2022-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: Sum of similar-triangle areas
smt-2022-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
$B_iC_i\parallel B_0C_0$, so $\triangle AB_iC_i\sim\triangle AB_0C_0$ with ratio $\frac{41-i}{41}$ and area $\left(\frac{41-i}{41}\right)^2[AB_0C_0]$. Triangle $B_iC_iC_{i+1}$ has the same base $B_iC_i$ as $AB_iC_i$ and its height is $\frac{1}{41-i}$ of the height (since $C_{i+1}$ is $1$ along a side of length $41-i$), so its area is $\frac1{41-i}\left(\frac{41-i}{41}\right)^2[AB_0C_0]=\frac{41-i}{41^2}[AB_0C_0]$.

Summing over $i=0,\dots,40$: $\sum_{j=1}^{41}\frac{j}{41^2}=\frac{41\cdot42/2}{41^2}=\frac{21}{41}$. The height of the big triangle is $\sqrt{41^2-9^2}=40$, area $\frac12\cdot18\cdot40=360$. Total coloured area: $\frac{21}{41}\cdot360=\frac{7560}{41}$.

**Answer: $\frac{7560}{41}$**

smt-2022-geometry-tiebreaker-02.title: Similar triangles with a common incentre
smt-2022-geometry-tiebreaker-02.body:
The line $D_1D_2$ is perpendicular to $ID$ (the common chord of two circles is perpendicular to the line of centres), so it is parallel to $BC$; similarly for the others. Hence the new triangle $XYZ$ is similar to $ABC$, and by symmetry $I$ is also its incentre. So the area ratio is the square of the ratio of inradii.

Let $M$ be where $D_1D_2$ meets $ID$ and $MD=x$. Then $D_1M^2=4-x^2$ and $IM=5-x$, and $D_1I=5$: $(4-x^2)+(5-x)^2=25\Rightarrow4-10x=0$, $x=\frac25$. The new inradius is $IM=5-\frac25=\frac{23}5$.

Ratio of areas $=\left(\frac{23/5}{5}\right)^2=\frac{529}{625}$.

**Answer: $\frac{529}{625}$**

smt-2022-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Isosceles triangle $TAC$
smt-2022-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $E$ be the foot of the altitude from $B$ (so $H\in BE$). Since $BA=BF$, $E$ is the midpoint of $AF$, so $HA=HF$ and $\angle HFA=\angle HAF=90^\circ-\angle C$. Hence $\angle HFC=180^\circ-\angle HFA=90^\circ+\angle C$, while $\angle HBC=90^\circ-\angle C$; these opposite angles sum to $180^\circ$, so $B,H,F,C$ are concyclic. By the power of the point $T$ with respect to this circle, $TB\cdot TC=TH\cdot TF$, so $\frac{TB}{TH}=\frac{TF}{TC}$ and (common angle at $T$) $\triangle TBF\sim\triangle THC$. As $TB=BF=8$, $\triangle TBF$ is isosceles with $\angle BTF=\angle BFT$, so the corresponding angles of $\triangle THC$ are equal and $HT=HC$.

Then $H$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $TC$; but $H$ also lies on the altitude from $A$, so the altitude from $A$ is the perpendicular bisector of $TC$, with $TC=BT+BC=18$. The foot $D$ of the altitude from $A$ satisfies $DC=9$, hence $BD=1$. Then $AD=\sqrt{AB^2-BD^2}=\sqrt{63}$, and $[ABC]=\frac12\cdot10\cdot\sqrt{63}=15\sqrt7$.

Check: $A=(1,\sqrt{63})$, $B=(0,0)$, $C=(10,0)$, $T=(-8,0)$: $BA=8<AC=12$, $F\in AC$ with $BF=8$, and $F,H,T$ are collinear.

**Answer: $15\sqrt7$**
